ばかり.en: ばかり highlights that 'nothing but (A) is being done', or 'only (A) exists'. We are looking for a grammar point that means 'so much...that' and is generally used in negative situations.

くらい.en: くらい expresses the limit of something in a similar way to ほど. We are looking for a grammar point that means 'so much...that' and is generally used in negative situations.

ばかりに.en: ばかり highlights that 'nothing but (A) is being done', or 'only (A) exists'. We are looking for a grammar point that means 'so much...that' and is generally used in negative situations.

そんなに.en: そんなに would be ungrammatical here since it needs to come before a verb or an adjective. We are looking for a grammar point that means 'so much...that' and is generally used in negative situations.

attributes.translation: When I was young, I studied so hard for an exam that there was a day when I was completely exhausted and I couldn't concentrate.(so much)
attributes.nuance_translation: A structure that often highlights an excessive amount of (A) that causes a negative result.

attributes.content: 先輩（せんぱい）は飲（の）み会（かい）でお酒（さけ）を沢山（たくさん）飲（の）んだ____、一人（ひとり）で帰（かえ）ることができなかった。
attributes.translation: Senpai drank so much at the party that he couldn't get home by himself.

attributes.content: 社長（しゃちょう）は社員（しゃいん）全員（ぜんいん）に恐（おそ）れられている____、誰（だれ）も社長（しゃちょう）の提案（ていあん）を否定（ひてい）しない。
attributes.translation: The CEO of our company is so feared by all of the workers that no one will criticize his decisions.

attributes.content: 最近（さいきん）彼女（かのじょ）と別（わか）れた友達（ともだち）を心配（しんぱい）する____、友達（ともだち）の話（はな）しを聞（き）きに行（い）った。
attributes.translation: I was so worried about my friend, who has broken up with his girlfriend recently, that I went to his place to listen to him vent.

attributes.body_ja:
名詞（めいし）の「あまり」は、「多（おお）すぎて残（のこ）った物（もの）」を意味（いみ）します。この「あまり」は、さまざまな品詞（ひんし）に付（つ）いて、多（おお）すぎたり、程度（ていど）が大（おお）きすぎたりすることが原因（げんいん）で、良（よ）くないことが起（お）こったことを表（あらわ）すときによく使（つか）われます。「余（あま）り」自体（じたい）にマイナスの意味（いみ）はありませんが、この文法（ぶんぽう）は良（よ）くないことに使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。

「あまり」は、動詞（どうし）や「さ」や「み」を使（つか）って名詞化（めいしか）したイ形容詞（けいようし）、「な」を付（つ）けたナ形容詞（けいようし）の語幹（ごかん）、または「の」を付（つ）けた名詞（めいし）のあとに続（つづ）けて使（つか）います。「あまり」のあとには主（おも）に、悪（わる）い出来事（できごと）を表（あらわ）す内容（ないよう）が続（つづ）きます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

文（ぶん）全体（ぜんたい）の時制（じせい）は、主節（しゅせつ）にある動詞（どうし）や形容詞（けいようし）の時制（じせい）で決（き）まるので、「あまり」の前（まえ）の形（かたち）は、現在形（げんざいけい）になったり、過去形（かこけい）になったりします。
attributes.body:
As a noun, あまり means 'excess', and refers to an amount of something that is in surplus. This noun is quite often used after many different types of words, to indicate that something happened/exists to an excessive degree (which then resulted in something negative occurring). By itself, 余（あま）り is not negative. However, this grammar point can be thought of as a set phrase that is generally used in negative situations.

To use あまり, you will need to attach it to the end of the following structures. A verb, an い-Adjective (that has been turned into a noun through the use of さ or み) followed by の, a な-Adjective followed by な, or a noun followed by の. Then, after あまり, a (B) phrase will highlight what the negative result was.

Caution

The tense of the overall sentence will be dependent on the main clause. Therefore, it is common to see the verb before あまり being used in several different tenses.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: What are the various uses of あまり?
接続・意味・使い方・例文

attributes.body: Both すぎる and あまり express that something is excessive, but they differ in usage and nuance. すぎる attaches to the stem of verbs and adjectives, while あまり follows plain-form verbs, nouns with の, or な-adjectives with な. Though すぎる can imply something negative, あまり more clearly emphasizes that the excess leads to a negative consequence.

あまり has the base meaning of 'excess', but its nuance changes with context. Together with a negative word in the form あまり～ない, it means 'not very (A)', e.g. あまり寒くない ('It's not very cold.'). Used affirmatively, it implies something of an excessive degree, e.g. 緊張のあまりうまくできなかった ('I was so nervous I couldn't do it well.').

first_relatable.title: あまり～ない
first_relatable.meaning: Not very, Not much, Not really, Hardly

attributes.body: Both express degree, but with different implications. なかなか implies something is quite or unexpectedly good, e.g. なかなかいい店だね ('This place is surprisingly good.') あまり highlights an excessive degree that leads to an unintended or negative result, e.g. 緊張のあまり声が震えた ('I was so nervous my voice shook.')

あまり follows a noun or verb phrase and shows that an extreme state leads to an unintended result, e.g. 緊張のあまり声が出なかった ('I was so nervous I couldn't speak.') からこそ attaches after the reason and emphasizes it as the precise cause, e.g. 緊張したからこそ全力を出せた ('It was precisely because I was nervous that I gave it my all.')

Both mean 'too much', but differ in nuance. あまりに emphasizes intensity and doesn't necessarily imply a result, e.g. あまりに暑い日だった ('It was an extremely hot day.') あまり highlights excess that leads to a (usually undesirable) outcome, e.g. 暑さのあまり眠れなかった ('I couldn't sleep due to the extreme heat.')

Both emphasize extremity, but with different focuses. Adjective + 限りだ expresses a strong feeling at its peak, e.g. 悲しい限りだ ('I'm as sad as can be.') あまり indicates that excess leads to a (usually undesirable) result, e.g. 悲しみのあまり声が出なかった ('I couldn't speak due to extreme sadness.')

first_relatable.title: Adj限りだ
first_relatable.meaning: Extremely, Really, Very, As ... as one can be

attributes.body: Both express emphasis, but in different ways. あまり is a noun that emphasizes an extreme degree leading to an unintended result, e.g. 悲しみのあまり泣き出した ('She burst into tears from too much sadness.') こそ is a particle that stresses importance or exclusivity, e.g. 今日こそ早く寝よう ('Today, for sure, I'll go to bed early.')

second_relatable.title: こそ
second_relatable.meaning: For sure, For certain, Even more so, Underlined or bolded text
